## Verdict

**Inkwell** costs least for a team of 22, at **$242 per month**. Its 20-seat minimum sits below the team size, so all 22 seats bill at the list rate of $11 with no padding. Dorado is $528 and Borealis $600 — Borealis despite having a lower per-seat rate than Dorado, because its 40-seat minimum forces payment for 18 unused seats.

## Vendor pricing

| Vendor | Price per seat | Minimum seats |
|---|---|---|
| Dorado | $24 | 5 |
| Inkwell | $11 | 20 |
| Borealis | $15 | 40 |

## Cost at this size

Seats paid for = the greater of 22 (team size) or the vendor minimum.

- **Dorado:** minimum 5 < 22, so 22 seats paid. 22 × $24 = **$528 per month**. Effective rate $24.00 per person.
- **Inkwell:** minimum 20 < 22, so 22 seats paid. 22 × $11 = **$242 per month**. Effective rate $11.00 per person.
- **Borealis:** minimum 40 > 22, so 40 seats paid. 40 × $15 = **$600 per month**. Effective rate $27.27 per person ($600 ÷ 22); 18 seats worth $270 go unused.

Inkwell is $286 per month cheaper than Dorado and $358 cheaper than Borealis — $3,432 and $4,296 per year.

## Risks

- **Inkwell's floor is close.** At 20 seats the minimum binds; a team shrinking below 20 still pays $220, raising the effective rate per person.
- **Borealis improves with growth, but never leads.** Its $600 is fixed until 40 seats, at which point it bills $15 per seat against Inkwell's $11 — so Inkwell stays cheapest at every size above 20 on list price.
- **Price only.** The list carries no feature, support, usage-limit or security detail, so a cheaper seat may buy less product. This ranking says nothing about fit.
- **Billing terms as stated.** Monthly billing at list. Annual commitments, volume discounts, onboarding or migration fees are not in the source and could reorder these figures.
